title: Odd tori of rings compose everywhere, even tori never reach the antipode; rings of cuts separate when they bound
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: On the square torus of equally spaced rings a contact needs a ring exactly when an odd number of contact-graph walks lead from it, counted by powers of x + 1/x + y + 1/y over GF(2), and every contact needs every ring on odd tori while none ever needs its antipodal ring on even tori. Cutting the contacts round any set of rings separates it, one ring of cuts round the torus does not, and two do.
